title: Make the evidence stages' apt bootstrap loud and https
body:
The v0.2.3 tag run died in the aarch64 evidence job with 56
mismatches that were not findings: every build in stage 3 had failed
with gcc and python3 not found, because the container's apt could not
fetch the toolchain and the bootstrap discarded apt's entire output.
The 16:53 gates run on main had already failed the same way, three
minutes after the same code passed on its pull request.

What the logs show, measured: on the aarch64 runner the alpine and
trixie stages kept working while the bullseye stage lost its
toolchain, in the same minute, over the same mirror host; the x86_64
evidence job was green at the same time. From outside, bullseye's
InRelease still verifies against bullseye's own keyring and its arm64
indices are all present. That leaves per-CDN-edge variance in the
bullseye repositories as the remaining explanation, and bullseye left
LTS on 2026-08-31, so churn there is expected while the suite migrates
toward archive.debian.org. The swallowed apt output was the only
witness that could have named the cause, and it was deleted.

Both Debian stage bootstraps now fetch over https with three retries,
keep their apt logs, and fail the stage naming the missing tool when
the toolchain does not install, instead of running a table whose every
case reports a mismatch about something else. The cross-compiler
install for section P stays best-effort with its own log, unchanged in
behaviour.

The failure path is proven locally with a stubbed failing apt-get and
no gcc on PATH: both stages exit 2 naming the tool and printing the
update and install logs. The success path is exercised by CI on this
pull request. No assertion in any experiment changed.

title: Ship all six architectures in the release, not just two
body:
The release workflow hardcoded x86_64 and aarch64 in the build matrix, the asset collection loop and the manifest verification loop, so v0.2.2 published only those two even though the gates already build six. This makes the matrix match the gates: x86_64, aarch64, riscv64, ppc64, ppc64le and loongarch64, both variants.

release-notes.sh refused on two floors, and loongarch64 builds on glibc 2.36 while the rest build on 2.31. The body now derives the floors from the manifests and states each architecture's floor, and still refuses when the two variants of one architecture disagree.

Verified: check-drift and check-charset exit 0; verify-gates proves all 14 gate bodies (clean tree, planted defects refuse, exemptions still green); release-notes.sh generates the mixed-floor header from synthetic manifests and refuses a two-floor architecture. The release workflow on this PR will build and package all six arches up to but not including publish.

title: Release all six architectures
body:
v0.2.2 shipped only x86_64 and aarch64 because the release workflow's
matrix, its collect step and its checksum step still enumerated two
architectures, and because scripts/release-notes.sh refused to generate
a body from manifests whose floors disagree, which they now do by
design: loongarch64's floor is glibc 2.36, the first release that runs
the architecture, against 2.31 everywhere else.

Widen all three to x86_64, aarch64, riscv64, ppc64, ppc64le and
loongarch64, and state the floor per architecture in the generated body
instead of once. The refusal survives in the scope where it was a
finding: the two variants of ONE architecture must still agree.

The collect step now refuses in both directions. Missing staged
artifacts already refused; an architecture that produced artifacts but
is not in the collect list now refuses too, so a matrix row added
without widening this list cannot ship a release that silently lacks
it, which is the shape v0.2.2 had.

Measured locally, with real builds:

- five cross builds plus one portable, packaged by package-release.sh;
  release-notes.sh generates the body from all six manifests with the
  per-arch floor table (aarch64 2.31 ... loongarch64 2.36), where the
  previous script exits 2 on the same input.
- planted defects, each seen to refuse: two manifests of one
  architecture disagreeing about the floor (exit 2); an unlisted s390x
  in staged (exit 1); a missing architecture (exit 1); one corrupted
  byte in a loose ppc64 asset against its manifest (exit 1, and 25 of
  25 pass clean).

The evidence gate is unchanged and still blocks every architecture: it
runs where it can, on the two architectures with runners, and the four
cross-compiled ones are released on the build verification, which the
workflow header now states with the pointer to
docs/report/10-measured-versus-assumed.md 10.

title: Support riscv64, ppc64, ppc64le and loongarch64 targets
body:
Add the four architectures end to end: the hand-written gl-fwd
trampolines (riscv64 and loongarch64 classic tail-jump forms; ppc64
split by ABI, ELFv2 TOC with a global entry for ppc64le and the ELFv1
.opd descriptor hop for big-endian), the loader and triplet names in
runtime-select and cross-libc-dlopen, the cross builds in
scripts/build.sh and build-in-env.sh, and CI rows that build all four.

Measurements behind it:

- Before this change, compiling src/gl-fwd.c for any of the four hit
  the "needs a tail-jump trampoline" error on gcc-10 and gcc-14; after
  it, make gl-fwd-asm-check assembles all five cross halves and make
  gl-fwd-qemu-check runs them under qemu-user: one argument of every
  register class through a trampoline, verified inside the target, a
  second call through the patched slot, a double return value, and the
  absent stub's zero in both the integer and the float return register.
  On ppc64 that includes the real ld64.so.1 walking .opd descriptors.
- Every artefact builds and passes scripts/verify-artifacts.sh on each
  architecture, floor glibc 2.31 on the bullseye cross toolchains and
  2.36 on loongarch64, which only exists from glibc 2.36 and needs the
  trixie cross compiler (gcc-10 has no loongarch64; checked against the
  Debian archive indices). build.sh selects that image by itself.
- The export-count check in the Makefile and verify-artifacts.sh moved
  from nm to readelf: an nm built without PowerPC reads ELFv1 .opd
  functions as data, and the count refused a correct ppc64 build
  (measured 0 against 3470).
- runtime-select's GLIBC_ version parse no longer uses sscanf: with
  _GNU_SOURCE and gcc 13 or newer, glibc redirects it to
  __isoc23_sscanf, which first exists in glibc 2.38, and the artefact
  silently needed 2.38 (measured on the gcc-14 loongarch64 build; the
  replacement parses identically on every version string shape,
  including wrap-around). loongarch64 now tops out at GLIBC_2.36.
- ld64 added to the never-touch list: the ppc64 loaders ld64.so.1
  (ELFv1) and ld64.so.2 (ELFv2) do not start with ld-linux.

Unverified, and stated in docs/report/10: the four architectures have
run under qemu-user and never on silicon, no host Mesa has been behind
the shims on them, and the AppImage evidence suite has no demo assets
for them. run-evidence.sh could not run on the machine that produced
this change (no container runtime available); CI runs it.

title: fix(gl-fwd): fall through to the next provider when the host has no target
body:
Fixes #28.

## What was wrong

On a host that ships `mesa-gl` but neither `mesa-egl` nor `mesa-gles`, `gles-fwd.so` found no forwarding target and kept all 358 entry points on zero-returning stubs. Because the preload wins symbol interposition and `.preload` lists `gles-fwd.so` ahead of `gl-fwd.so`, those stubs shadowed every GL 1.x name the two tables share. Contour drives desktop GL over GLX: the context was real (made through `gl-fwd.so` and the host's `libGL.so.1`), but the direct `glGetString(GL_VERSION)` call landed on the stub and returned NULL, which contour reports as `Unrecognized OpenGL version ((null):0, (null))` before rendering a black window.

`LD_DEBUG=bindings` settled which object won:

```
binding file .../libQt6Gui.so.6 ... to .../cross-libc-dlopen/gles-fwd.so: normal symbol `glGetString'
```

## The repair

One pass in `glfwd_fill_addr` (`src/gl-fwd.c`): when the shim has no target, ask `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, name)` once per name. A name the process can still serve from behind the shim is served from there, which is exactly what the application would have bound to had the shim not been preloaded. A miss keeps the absent stub, so the zero-returning contract survives where nothing sits behind.

A shim that refuses to forward to itself keeps the whole table absent exactly as before: that refusal answers a misconfigured lookup, not an absent host, and E68 measures it. The two paths are separated by one flag, and the refusal was fired again by hand against the five-name miniature with the repair in place.

The with-target path is untouched: the new pass runs only when `glfwd_target` is NULL.

## What was measured

- **Fails before, passes after.** E75c (new) preloads a no-target shim beside a linked provider: before the repair the stub shadowed it (`ints=0`), after the repair the call lands on the provider (`ints=205`). E75d is the no-preload control, E75e pins the new log line.
- `sh scripts/run-evidence.sh`: **62/62 on x86-64, exit 0.** The same tree with only the cases added scored 60/62, E75c and E75e the only mismatches.
- **The real application.** Contour `0.7.0.8982-1` on the Alpine host, shims built from this tree on the glibc 2.31 floor: `no target; 358 of 358 entry points fall through to the next provider in scope`, no version warning, the window renders. The shims at `main` log `no target; all 358 entry points return zero` and render black.
- **With-target regression check.** On a glvnd glibc host where `libGLESv2.so.2` exists: `358 of 358 entry points resolved from the host library`, unchanged from `main`.
- **Self-refusal.** Still refuses, all five miniature entry points absent, exit 1.

The aarch64 total (59/59) is the x86-64 table minus the three named skips (E22, E23, E58); the ARM job on this pull request is the measurement.

## Why the AppImage suite cannot flip

Every host stage installs a full GL stack (`43-host-alpine.sh` installs `mesa-egl mesa-gles`, `44-host-debian.sh` installs `libegl-mesa0 libegl1`, `46-host-ubuntu.sh` installs `libegl1-mesa`), so on those hosts the forwarding shims find targets and the new branch never runs. E68, E72, E73 and E74 pin the refusal, the absent report, the call count and the lazy load, and none of their predictions moved.

## Documentation

`docs/report/09-the-second-boundary.md` 9.20 records the real-application measurement with both outputs and both controls. `docs/diagnostics.md` documents the new debug line beside the old one. `README.md` states the behavior where the shims are introduced. The evidence-suite totals move from 53/53 and 50/50 to 62/62 and 59/59 (the tree has run 62 cases since the libva cases landed), and the one-home list in `gates.yml` follows them.

## Review passes

- Pass 1, does every claim added here hold when the command is run: every quoted output in 9.20 was re-checked against the captured logs, which caught one quote carrying the issue's spacing rather than the program's. Fixed.
- Pass 2, what did this change stop measuring: nothing. The zero-returning contract still has its two measured shapes (nothing behind the shim: E75b; refused self: E68), the with-target absent report and the lazy load are pinned by E72 through E74, and no assertion greps a line whose meaning moved.

title: docs: overhaul the README and retire the fork dependency
body:
## What changed

**README overhaul.** The README read like a machine wrote it. It has been rewritten in plainer prose a new reader can follow, with the two-gap framing kept because that is the part people actually need.

**Where it has been tested.** New section: Ubuntu 12.04 through 22.04, Alpine Linux, Arch Linux, Artix Linux, NixOS and Slackware, all working.

**Known limitations.** New section after the tested list, covering the three places where the host's Mesa is the ceiling and this project cannot raise it:

- a GTK4 application needs `glBufferStorage` (desktop GL 4.4 / `GL_ARB_buffer_storage` / `GL_EXT_buffer_storage`), which Mesa 10.1 on Ubuntu 14.04 lacks
- OpenGL 4.6 arrived with Mesa 20.0 (Feb 2020, radeonsi), so a system on Mesa 19.x or older stops at 4.5
- Vulkan 1.3 arrived with Mesa 22.0 (Mar 2022, RADV and ANV), so older distributions cannot run an application that demands 1.3 or 1.4

The OpenGL and Vulkan version claims were verified against the Mesa release notes before writing. Note this corrects the original suggestion: OpenGL 4.6 landed in Mesa 20.0, which is Ubuntu 20.04, not 22.04.

**The fork dependency is gone.** Upstream `pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages` now publishes the `host-drivers` demo assets that previously existed only on the `Samueru-sama/Anylinux-AppImages` fork. Both orchestrators take every asset from the upstream.

**The demo pins are gone, because the tag is rolling.** The `demo` tag is mutable, so a checked-in SHA was stale the moment it was written. Both orchestrators now read the digest the release API publishes at download time and verify the bytes against it:

- `scripts/run-appimage.sh` and `experiments/appimage.ps1` carry no sha256 pin at all; `scripts/suite-lib.sh` `fetch_verified` and the PowerShell side both query the release API. A cached copy is re-verified and re-downloaded when the tag moved.
- `scripts/check-drift.sh` section 3b refuses a leftover 64-hex digest in either orchestrator and checks both verify the same upstream repo and tag.

**Docs kept consistent.** Report 9.15/9.17, ground-truth, reproducing, integrating, PROGRESS, infrastructure T-10, the appimage-suite cache comment and the secret-sweep narrowing all describe live verification instead of pins. The measured record keeps its numbers and gets the corrected premise underneath, per the repo rule.

## Verification

- `sh scripts/check-drift.sh` exit 0, with both new failure paths (leftover digest, divergent upstream) planted and seen to refuse
- `sh scripts/check-charset.sh` exit 0
- Template `check-docs.sh` and `check-control-bytes.sh` clean
- `sh -n` on every tracked `.sh` and a pwsh parse of `appimage.ps1` pass
- Live `fetch_verified` run against the real release API for all three assets, covering stale-cache re-download and matching-cache reuse

title: fix(egl-fwd): derive __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_DIRS from XDG_DATA_DIRS
body:
Fixes #23.

## What

On NixOS `eglgears_x11` and `eglgears_wayland` die with `EGLUT: failed to initialize EGL display`, while `vkcube` and `glxgears` work. The trace in the issue shows why: `egl-fwd.so` ends at `bundled dispatcher (nothing better on this host)`, resolves 44 of 44 entry points, and `eglInitialize` then fails, because a glvnd dispatcher with no vendor behind it has no EGL implementation to initialize.

## Root cause

The bundled dispatcher is upstream libglvnd, and libglvnd finds a host's EGL vendors only through `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_DIRS`, or the datadir compiled into it (`src/EGL/libeglvendor.c`). That compiled default is the BUILD host's `/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d`, which NixOS does not have: the vendor json lives under `/run/opengl-driver/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d`, and the launcher publishes that root through `XDG_DATA_DIRS` (Anylinux-sharun `set_share_env`). sharun also derives `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_DIRS` from `XDG_DATA_DIRS`, but only for a bundle that ships its own mesa or glvnd share directory (`SHARUN_MESA_PATH`). A host-drivers AppImage has neither by construction, so the derivation never fires, and the gap lands on the shim.

GLX masks the same gap with libglvnd's indirect fallback, which is why `glxgears` "works"; EGL has no such fallback.

## The fix

`glfwd_set_egl_vendor_env()` in `src/gl-fwd.c`, called from both bundled-target branches of `glfwd_open_target`: probe `<dir>/glvnd/egl_vendor.d` for every entry of `XDG_DATA_DIRS` and set the variable when it is unset. Only the EGL and GLES shims do this (`GLFWD_VENDOR_DIR` is NULL for GL, and GLES dispatches through the EGL vendor mechanism). Guards: an existing value is never clobbered (a user's or launcher's choice wins), non-absolute XDG entries are skipped, and a host with no vendor directory at all is left on the compiled default rather than pointed at an empty list.

`LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` stays in `cross-libc-dlopen.c` on purpose: libva is loaded by AppImages that carry no GL shims at all, and that derivation must fire with no GL entry point ever called.

## Measured

In a `nixos/nix` container (real nix store; nixpkgs `mesa` 26.2.1 and `libglvnd` 1.7.0; the vendor json placed where ONLY `XDG_DATA_DIRS` reaches it, so a dispatcher without the variable cannot find it by default):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| egl-fwd target | `bundled dispatcher (nothing better on this host)` | same target, plus `__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_DIRS=.../glvnd/egl_vendor.d, from XDG_DATA_DIRS` |
| `eglInitialize` | fails (issue #23's trace, reproduced) | succeeds; the host mesa vendor loads and the full config and context sequence runs |
| fixed shim with `XDG_DATA_DIRS` unset | n/a | behaves exactly like before (control) |
| FHS desktop host (glvnd, real vendor directory) | works | byte-identical behavior to before |

`make` stays clean (`gl-fwd-verify` counts unchanged: 3470 / 44 / 358) and `sh scripts/check-drift.sh` stays green.

## Notes for review

- The container measurement is a faithful layout simulation (real nix store, real nixpkgs graphics packages), not a full NixOS boot. Confirmation on real NixOS hardware is one rebuild plus `eglgears_x11` away.
- Left out deliberately: the GLX analog (`glx_vendor.d`), a NixOS suite stage with the FHS paths deleted (T-05's technique), and any `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH` work: host mesa self-locates its DRI drivers (nixpkgs compiles the absolute store path in), and the bundled-mesa case belongs to sharun's `SHARUN_MESA_PATH`.

body:
## What and why

VA-API was classified an unmeasured plugin boundary (`tools/plugin_boundaries.py:88`): bundled `libva.so.2` dlopens `<name>_drv_video.so` from the host. On the way to measuring it, one half of the problem turned out to be unfixable by the existing mechanism and is repaired here.

`libva` never opens its driver by soname. `va_openDriver()` (va/va.c) colon-splits `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` (or a `VA_DRIVERS_PATH` compiled into the running libva) and opens the **constructed absolute path**. A bundled libva carries its build host's dri layout, and no `--library-path` can correct that, because no soname lookup ever happens.

## The change

`src/cross-libc-dlopen.c` gains a guarded `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` assembler:

- **Only when libva is loaded.** `dl_iterate_phdr` for soname prefix `libva.so.`, from the constructor (startup-linked libva: ffmpeg, mpv, browsers) and after every successful interposed `dlopen` until it fires (libva entering as a dependency of a dlopened plugin: gstreamer's va plugin). Either route has fired before `vaInitialize` can read the variable.
- **Host dri dirs only.** Probed as `<dir>/dri` under the process's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (host entries, via the existing `is_host_library_path` boundary) and the conventional libdirs (triplet, lib64, lib, local). Never `$APPDIR/lib/dri`: a bundle that ships VA drivers manages the variable itself, and its entries stay ahead of anything appended here.
- **Appended, never clobbered.** Existing value keeps the front of libva's walk, the same place the conventions put appended path entries. Deduped against what is already set.
- Honors `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN=0` and `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN_DRYRUN=1` (reports, does not set), one `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN_DEBUG` line naming the final value.
- ⛔ Nothing here opens a library (`docs/conventions/code.md`): appending directories to a search list is not searching it. libva does its own searching from the result.

## The guard is "settled", not "ran" — measured, not designed

The first revision latched the guard when the constructor found no libva, which permanently disarmed the post-dlopen scan; E97 failed exactly that way and the fix is in the comment. The scan re-runs per successful dlopen until libva turns up.

## The case (FAILS before, PASSES after)

Section Q of `experiments/30-run-tests.sh`, E95 through E100: a fake `libva.so.2` implementing `va_openDriver`'s contract, stand-in drivers that answer with the directory they were built for, and the answer round-tripped through the driver's own function, so a pass is not "a string appeared".

| | from `main` | with the change |
|---|---|---|
| E95 startup-linked libva finds the host driver | MISMATCH | MATCH |
| E96 control, `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN=0` | MATCH (FAIL as predicted) | MATCH |
| E97 late load through a dlopened plugin | MISMATCH | MATCH |
| E98 user-set value kept first, ours appended | MISMATCH | MATCH |
| E99 bundle dri never enters the list | MISMATCH | MATCH |
| E100 no libva, variable untouched | MATCH | MATCH |

Full evidence table on this branch: **59/59 on x86-64** (`debian:bullseye-slim`, glibc 2.31), every prior prediction still held.

## A finding on the way (docs/traps.md)

An interposed `dlopen` consults the **interposer's** `DT_RPATH`/`DT_RUNPATH`, not the calling binary's. A soname reachable only through the caller's own runpath stops resolving under the preload. The trap entry names the two ways out (library path, or dlopen an object that NEEDs it).

## Documentation

- `docs/integrating.md`: a VA-API section under "Per target".
- ⚠ **Still UNVERIFIED, stated as such in the doc**: a real `iHD_drv_video.so` or `i965_drv_video.so` carried across a libc boundary. That needs a host with one installed; E95-E100 measure the search-list half with a stand-in driver.

## Reconciliation owed at close-out

`docs/report/08-test-results.md` Tier 1 says 53/53 on x86-64 and 50/50 on aarch64, citing its CI run. This branch makes the x86-64 total 59; the aarch64 total needs CI's run before the report is updated, and the six new cases are architecture-independent C, so no skip path was added.

title: fix(gles-fwd): resolve GLES from host EGL on classic hosts
body:
Fixes #21.

## What

On a classic host (musl Alpine) there is no `libGLESv2.so.2` and no glvnd vendor, so `gles-fwd.so` fell through its target selection to the **bundled glvnd dispatcher**. That dispatcher has no vendor behind it, so its GLES entry points are no-ops: `glGetString` returns NULL, everything else returns zero. GTK4's renderer is GLES, so `gtk4-demo` died (SIGFPE/SIGSEGV) instead of drawing.

The fix adds `GLFWD_ALT_SONAME`: a shim can name a second SONAME to look for when the primary one is absent from the host. `gles-fwd` sets it to `libEGL.so.1`, because classic Mesa folds GLES into `libEGL` and reaches it through `eglGetProcAddress` — which is exactly what `GLFWD_GETPROC` already names for this shim, so `glfwd_fill_addr` needs no other change. `gl-fwd` and `egl-fwd` leave it unset (NULL) and are unchanged.

## Measured

On `alpine:3.22`, running the host-drivers `gtk4-demo` AppImage under xvfb:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| exit | rc=136 (SIGFPE) | rc=143 (still running) |
| gles-fwd target | bundled dispatcher ("nothing better") | host EGL library |
| GLES resolved | 358/358 (no-ops) | 358/358 via `eglGetProcAddress`, 0 absent |
| GLES entry points called | 2 | 46 |

New cases `E91`-`E94` in `experiments/50-gtk4-host-drivers.sh` (plus extractor `49-*` and `--only gtk4hd` wiring in `run-appimage.sh`) fail with the previous shim and pass with this one. `sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` stays 53/53.

## Note for review

`docs/report/10-measured-versus-assumed.md` records the GLES-on-classic-host repair as "measured, not repaired" (bullet at the top of section 10). This change repairs and measures it (E91-E94), so that bullet and the report counts will need reconciling under the "one fact, one home" rule; I left the report alone here to keep the change scoped to the code and the case.

title: State the floor rule against the glibc that decides it, and expose make portable
body:
Closes #13. Supersedes #12, whose README simplification is carried here with the numbering fixed.

Stacked on #18.

## The floor rule named the wrong variable

#13 reports that the rule reads as forbidding a build on a new glibc, and that the vkcube demo is built on Arch and drives Ubuntu 12.04's OpenGL drivers anyway. Both halves of that are correct, and the conclusion that the paragraph should be deleted is not. The rule is real; it was stated against the wrong thing.

**Measured, building on glibc 2.43:**

```
$ objdump -T cross-libc-dlopen.so | grep -oE 'GLIBC_2\.[0-9]+' | sort -uV | tail -1
GLIBC_2.34
```

`dlopen`, `dlsym`, `dlclose`, `dladdr`, `dlvsym` and `dlinfo` moved into libc at glibc 2.34, and `stat` and `fstat` at 2.33. The same source built on `debian:bullseye-slim` needs at most `GLIBC_2.16`.

⭐ **What decides it is the glibc the consuming process CARRIES, never the host's.** These objects are preloaded into somebody else's process. A host running a fifteen-year-old distribution is irrelevant to whether they load, which is the whole point of the project. The demo works built on Arch because the AppImage it goes into bundles glibc 2.44, not because Ubuntu 12.04 is old.

⛔ It still breaks in one direction: a build on 2.43 needs `GLIBC_2.34`, and a bundle carrying 2.31 does not have it. That is why the default is a container and the floor is 2.31.

The rule now reads **"build on a glibc no newer than the oldest BUNDLED glibc you will load into"**, and says plainly that building on the newest is correct whenever every bundle you target is at least as new. Restated in `README.md`, `docs/building.md` and `scripts/build.sh`'s header, each with the measurement.

## `make portable`, so nobody has to patch this repository

#13 also reports that `--portable` is undocumented and that downstream reaches it by patching the Makefile:

```
sed -i -e 's/ -fcf-protection=full//' Makefile
```

That is a patch against this repository because it had no other way to say no. It does now:

```bash
cd src && make portable
```

No container, no build script. It is `sh scripts/build.sh --portable` with the orchestration removed, and produces the same objects. `docs/building.md` gains a section documenting it, both flags, and `--portable` itself, which appeared in no document before.

⛔ **The Makefile now asks the compiler instead of assuming from the architecture.** Targeting x86 is not the same as supporting `-fcf-protection=full`: a toolchain built without CET refuses it on x86 too, and the architecture test alone let that reach the compiler as a hard error. That is the reason the `sed` existed, and most callers now need neither it nor `make portable` for that purpose.

## Two things found while doing it

**`src/Makefile` cited a `scripts/build.sh --strict-env` option that has never existed.** Nothing broke because nothing ran it. A citation of a flag is not checked the way a citation of a path is.

**Dropping the CET flag removes the request, not always the instructions.** A toolchain that enables CET by default still emits `endbr64`, and that is the distribution's choice rather than this project's. Measured on a gcc whose `-Q --help=common` reports `-fcf-protection=full`: the default and portable builds carry 202 each, identical. The documentation says so rather than implying the instructions go away.

## From #12

The README opening is @Samueru-sama's, kept close to their wording: it names `cross-libc-dlopen.so` at the point where gap 1 is introduced, and says up front that musl-linked drivers work.

⚠ **Their split of the one table into two left the prose numbering behind.** The tail of the old sentence, `2 is repaired by an object built with the SONAME...`, stayed as a bare paragraph with no "Gap 2" in front of it. Both halves are now labelled **Gap 1** and **Gap 2** beside their own tables. The `has has` typo is fixed.

⚠ **Two measured caveats #12 removed are kept**: that this is a preload rather than an AppImage feature, and that a non-AppImage process against a real GPU driver is UNVERIFIED. The second is the open entry T-03, and dropping it would make the page claim something nobody has run.

I have not pushed to the fork. `docs/conventions/git.md` section 4 forbids writing to any repository but this one, so this supersedes #12 rather than amending it.

## Measured

`sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` reports 53 of 53 MATCH, identical case for case to the baseline on `main` at `df11f5fb`.

`cd src && make portable` builds all five artefacts, with `-DCLD_STRICT_ENV` and zero requests for the CET flag. The default build still requests it three times on this compiler.

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` passes, and its documented-make-target check now covers `portable`. Every `build.sh --<option>` the documents name is one the script parses, which `--strict-env` was not.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 14 gates, 0 not.

title: Add the entry points, write down the layout rule, and teach the cited-path check to read comments
body:
Stacked on #17, and the last of the five. Two entry documents, the layout rule that was never written down, and a check extension that found two stale citations on its first run.

## The entry points

`CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` are the two files a visitor opens without following a link: GitHub offers the first when a pull request is opened and surfaces the second on the security tab.

⛔ **`CONTRIBUTING.md` states no rule of its own.** It is a table of links into `docs/conventions/`, which is the authority, plus the three commands to run before opening a pull request. A rule written twice disagrees with itself, which is what #16 spent its diff undoing.

`SECURITY.md` names GitHub's private advisory form and says what is worth reporting for this project specifically: a way to open a path the bundle does not own, to escape `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, to get a second libc into the process, or to make a shim forward to something other than the one soname it impersonates. ⚠ It says plainly that a crash is worth reporting even when nobody has shown it is exploitable, because this code parses ELF files it did not produce.

⚠ **`docs/security.md` answers a different question** and now says so in its first paragraph, with a link both ways. That page is about what a pull request can reach in CI. This one is about a defect in the code.

## The layout rule

The root holds code, tooling and those three documents. Everything written for a reader is under `docs/`.

⚠ **This had never been written down.** `HISTORY/` and `TODO/` sat at the root, in capitals, beside `src/` and `tests/` for the life of the project, and no rule said they should not. #17 moved them; this states the rule and adds section 4b of `check-drift.sh`, which refuses a fourth markdown file at the root. Proven by planting one.

## The cited-path check now reads comments

`check-drift.sh` section 2 verified every repository path cited in a document. It never looked at code, and **a comment citing a moved file is as stale as a link to one**.

Widened to C, shell, Python, YAML and Makefile comments. Measured: **68 repository paths are cited from comments, and two did not exist.**

| stale citation | where | why it survived |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/REPORT.md` | `src/Makefile:103` | left by the split in #17, because the rewriter walked Markdown and a Makefile comment is not Markdown |
| `tools/lib/anylinux.c` | `src/cross-libc-dlopen.c:27` | not stale at all: the anchor matched the tail of `useful-tools/lib/anylinux.c`, which is upstream's path |

The first is fixed. The second was a false positive in the check itself, so the anchor now refuses to match a path that is the tail of a longer word, rather than being exempted by name.

Four more are exempt by name, each verified first: three are built binaries cited in their own source's usage line (`tests/abi-host`, `tests/cudaprobe`, `tests/soak`, whose `.c` files are all tracked), and one belongs to `Azathothas/TEMPLATE` and is fetched at a URL named on the same line.

⚠ **A code span is stripped from a comment too.** A comment naming a path that deliberately does not exist is recording a finding rather than citing a file, and this script's own section 2 comment does exactly that when it records that `scripts/check-prose-dashes.sh` was cited for a whole branch and never existed. Backticks are how the two are told apart, in a comment as in a document.

Cited paths checked went **91 to 113**.

## And a second class the move had hidden

⛔ **A link's target resolving is not enough. Its text is what a reader
believes.** A link reads `[the/path/shown](the/path/followed)`, and only the
second half was ever checked.

Found by sweeping for it: when `HISTORY/` moved under `docs/` in #17, two links
in `docs/todo/measurement.md` kept `HISTORY/references/...` as their **text**
while their targets were rewritten correctly. Every check passed, the template's
link checker passed, and both pages went on showing a reader a directory that
no longer exists.

Both are fixed, and section 2d refuses the next one. ⚠ **Only text containing a
slash is read**, which is what makes the check usable rather than noisy: eleven
links here use a bare filename as a short label, and `[`code.md`](code.md)` is
not a claim about where the file lives. A slash turns the text into a claim
about the tree, and a claim can be wrong.

Two exemptions, both measured rather than assumed. A fenced block, because the
page that states this rule has to show the shape it is about. And a link whose
target is a URL, because `Azathothas/TEMPLATE` as link text is an owner and a
repository, not a path here; six links are written that way.

## One check deliberately not added

The task list called for an unreachable-page check. ⛔ **It already exists and is not duplicated here.** The template's fetched `check-docs.sh` resolves every relative link and reports a page nothing links to. Run against this tree: 52 files, 378 relative links, clean. A second implementation would be a second thing to keep in step, and the first to drift.

## A correction inside the measured record

Section 9.14 records a dash ratchet that drifted eight under the tree and then admitted a planted dash. #15 replaced that ratchet with a refusal, so the section described a mechanism that no longer exists.

Per `docs/conventions/prose.md`, a premise a later change disproves keeps its title and gets the correction written underneath, because the title is how the item is cited everywhere else. The correction says what section 4 does now and leaves the measurements in the tense they were written in, since they are the reason for the change.

## Measured

`sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` reports 53 of 53 MATCH, identical case for case to the baseline on `main` at `df11f5fb`.

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` passes: 113 cited paths exist, no dash used as punctuation, 3 entry documents at the root, and all 15 entries reconcile.

`sh scripts/check-charset.sh` passes over 138 tracked files.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 12 gates, 0 not.

The template's `check-docs.sh`, patched the way CI patches it, reports 52 files and 378 relative links clean.

title: Move the history and open-work records under docs/, and split the report by section
body:
Stacked on #16. The root now holds code, tooling and one entry document. Everything a person reads lives under `docs/`.

```
before                        after
------                        -----
HISTORY/                      docs/history/
TODO/                         docs/todo/
docs/REPORT.md   2995 lines   docs/report/   12 sections + an index
```

## The moves

`HISTORY/` and `TODO/` sat at the root in capitals, beside `src/` and `tests/`, which put prose and code at the same level. Both move under `docs/`. All 13 files are recorded as pure renames with no content change.

**80 references were rewritten**, and the depth of a relative link changes with the file that holds it, so this was not a string substitution. Each link was resolved against its old directory and re-expressed against its new one. Measured after: **0 broken relative links anywhere in the tree**.

## The split

`docs/REPORT.md` was 2995 lines, so a citation of section 9.14 sent a reader to a document rather than to a page. It becomes `docs/report/`, one file per numbered section, with `docs/report/README.md` as the index.

Section numbers are preserved because the rest of the repository cites them. **All 39 subsection numbers are present after the split, and the set is identical to before.** 129 citations were rewritten, each to the page holding the section it names, with the subsection number left as written.

⚠ **Section 9 stays whole at 1386 lines.** Its subsections are cited by number from across the repository, and splitting one topic across several pages makes `9.14` ambiguous about which page to open. The design left this decidable at split time; this is the decision and the reason.

⛔ **The index carries no measured value.** It names sections and says what each covers, because a count repeated there would be a second home for a value that is supposed to have one.

## Three things the checks caught, and one premise of mine that was wrong

**The one-fact-one-home gate failed on the split.** It counts files, and the report went from one file to twelve, so six headline numbers appeared to have several homes while nothing had drifted. Every occurrence is inside `docs/report/`, verified. The gate now collapses those pages to one home rather than excluding them, which is the distinction that matters: a number appearing in the report **and** in any other document still refuses, and that is the case the gate exists for. `scripts/verify-gates.sh` carries the same change, and still proves the gate fires.

**The cited-path check read 0 after the move**, which looks exactly like the silent-narrowing failure this repository's own notes warn about: a check that stops recognising a class of citation reports success over a smaller set. It was a stale index rather than a real narrowing, and the true count went **89 to 91** across this change. The `anchor` regex is simplified anyway, because `docs` already covers `docs/todo` and `docs/history` and naming them again is two more chances to drift. A planted citation of a path that does not exist is refused.

**The `docs()` helper and the `gates.yml` exclusion** both named `HISTORY/*` literally. Left alone they would have begun scanning the record they were written to exclude, which is loud rather than silent, but they are updated in the same change as the move because a rename without them leaves a tree where documented paths do not resolve.

⚠ **A premise in the proposal for this work was wrong and is corrected rather than dropped.** It claimed `REPORT.md` carried pasted WSL output whose `#` lines Markdown parsed as top-level headings. Both such passages are already inside fenced blocks. A fence-aware reading of the file gives exactly 13 headings, the title and 12 numbered sections, so the outline was never broken and nothing is fenced here.

## Measured

`sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` reports 53 of 53 MATCH, identical case for case to the baseline on `main` at `df11f5fb`.

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` passes: 91 cited paths exist, no dash used as punctuation, and all 15 entries reconcile against `docs/todo/INDEX.md`.

`sh scripts/check-charset.sh` passes over 136 tracked files.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 12 gates, 0 not.

Every page under `docs/report/` is linked from the index, and the index is linked from `README.md` and `docs/AGENTS.md`.

⛔ **Breaking for anything holding a link.** Every external link into `HISTORY/`, `TODO/` or `docs/REPORT.md` changes. The merged pull requests #8, #10 and #11 cite those paths in their bodies and are not rewritten.

title: Say it once: merge a duplicated file header, and stop RULES.md restating the conventions
body:
Stacked on #15. One theme: **say it once.** A source file stated its purpose twice, and a rules document restated three whole sections of the conventions it was supposed to defer to.

## In the code

**`src/cross-libc-dlopen.c` stated its purpose twice**, at lines 1 to 17 and again at 56 to 72. The second block carried two facts the header did not, namely that a host object's version requirements are stripped from a private memfd copy, and that anything outside the bundle root counts as a host library. Both are merged into the header and the duplicate is gone.

**A comment narrated a change instead of stating a contract.** It read "Before this change those arms could rely on the variable being unset; now they must say 0, and they do", which tells a reader nothing they can act on. It now says what an arm that leaves the variable unset actually measures.

One smaller fix: `// print to stderr when CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN_DEBUG=1` sat above the predicate function rather than the macro it described.

## In the documents

`docs/conventions/README.md` calls itself the authority, and `docs/AGENTS.md` says it "restates nothing written elsewhere, so the two cannot fork". `TODO/RULES.md` forked anyway. Measured before this change: **8 sentences appeared verbatim in more than one document**, and three whole sections of `RULES.md` were near-copies of `docs/conventions/git.md`.

| section of `RULES.md` | where that content actually lives |
|---|---|
| Attribution | `git.md` section 1, near-verbatim |
| Repository permissions | `git.md` section 4, near-verbatim |
| Publishing | `git.md` sections 2 and 3 |
| Working method | `code.md` tests rules, `prose.md` on measured versus estimated |
| Rules that must not be broken | partly `README.md`'s invariants, partly nowhere else |

That last row is the one that mattered. The implementation invariants were real content with no other home, sitting in a file about tracking work rather than beside the code they govern. They move to `docs/conventions/code.md`, which is what governs `src/`, as two new sections: the invariants themselves, and the rule that finding libraries is `ld.so`'s job with `gl-fwd.c`'s single-soname lookup as the one bounded exception.

`RULES.md` goes from 149 lines to 66 and now owns one thing, the life of an entry in that directory: what an entry is, that it closes in place, and the close-out sequence. Everything else is a table of links.

Two smaller restatements went with it. `docs/limits.md` reproduced `prose.md`'s SKIP rule in its opening paragraph and now cites it. `TODO/measurement.md` T-01 restated `limits.md`'s three static-linking rows as its own premise and now points at them, which also means the closure rewrites one place instead of two.

**Measured after: 0 sentences appear in more than one document.**

## Two corrections to rules landed in #15

⛔ Both would have destroyed something, and both were found by trying to apply them.

**"One comment syntax per file" would have forced a conventional header into churn.** Taken literally, the majority syntax wins, which in `cross-libc-dlopen.c` means rewriting a `/* */` file header into 28 lines of `//`. The rule now exempts the header and records that no file in `src/` mixes the two.

**"A comment is not a changelog" would have deleted the two best comments in the repository.** `src/cld-env.h` explains why the deprecated `ANYLINUX_*` aliases were removed and what two names for one control cost. `scripts/build-in-env.sh` explains why an `apt-get update` failure is fatal on its own. Both read like history and neither is: each names a failure mode that returns the moment somebody undoes the decision. The rule now separates a narration, which says what happened, from a rationale, which says what will happen to the next person who tries the obvious thing.

## Three sweeps that found nothing

⚠ Recorded because a pass with no findings owes the reader what it swept.

**No comment restates the line below it.** A word-overlap sweep over `src/`, `tests/`, `tools/` and `scripts/` flagged two candidates, both false positives on macro continuation lines.

**No file mixes comment syntax.**

**No changelog comment survives outside the one fixed above.**

The C in this repository is not where the slop was. Comment density is 22% in `cross-libc-dlopen.c` and 18% in `runtime-select.c`, and the large blocks are file headers.

## Measured

`sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` reports 53 of 53 MATCH, identical case for case to the baseline on `main` at `df11f5fb`.

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` and `sh scripts/check-charset.sh` both pass, which matters because a rewritten comment can reintroduce a dash.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 12 gates, 0 not.

The only behaviour-bearing file touched is `src/cross-libc-dlopen.c`, and every hunk in it is inside a comment.

title: Refuse non-ASCII characters and dashes used as punctuation
body:
Stacked on #14, which cleared the tree. This change states the two rules and lands the checks that refuse them, armed over every tracked file at once. There is no scope list and no phase where a check merely suggests.

⭐ **This pull request is the test of #14.** Arming a check over a tree the previous change cleaned is how the completeness of that change gets checked by a machine rather than asserted by whoever ran it. Both checks pass, so nothing was missed.

## The rules

`docs/conventions/prose.md` gains a character-set rule and tightens the dash rule:

- ASCII only, with `⛔ ⭐ ⚠ ✅ ❌` as the sole exception, each removed character listed with its ASCII spelling.
- No dash as punctuation in any spelling, not only the em dash.
- A rule is a complete sentence, with a subject and a verb.

`docs/conventions/code.md` gains a comment rule: a comment carries what the code cannot say, a file states its purpose once, a comment is not a changelog, one comment syntax per file, and a defect in a generated file is fixed at its generator.

## The checks

`scripts/check-charset.sh` is new. It refuses any character outside ASCII that is not one of the five markers, reporting the file, the line and the code point.

`scripts/check-drift.sh` section 4 stops being a ratchet. `BUDGET` is gone. It refuses, carries no tolerance, and does not pass because a count fell. `docs/REPORT.md` 9.14 records why: the pin drifted eight under the tree across three commits and then admitted a planted dash, because the only thing asking anyone to lower it was a suggestion the script printed.

Its scope widens from Markdown to C, shell, Python, YAML and Makefile comments, and it now catches a dash that wraps at the end of a line. That last one had never been counted: the pattern required a trailing space, so a paragraph breaking straight after the dash was invisible for the whole life of the ratchet.

## What both checks deliberately permit

- **A specimen in a code span.** Without this the rules are unwritable: a page banning a character cannot show which one, and `scripts/verify-gates.sh` cannot record the plant that proves the check fires. Both exemptions are themselves proven on every run, because an exemption nobody checks can stop applying in silence.
- **An end-of-options separator** such as `cd --` or `git grep --`, 31 in the tree.
- **A command synopsis** such as `NAME -- CMD [ARGS...]`. `src/runtime-select.c:36` documents its own CLI that way, and a C comment has no backticks for the code-span exemption to reach.
- **A banner line** such as `# ----- name --`, which divides sections rather than punctuating a sentence.
- **`HISTORY/`**, which records original wording.

## What they deliberately do not cover

Prose inside strings a program prints, 106 occurrences. The check records the gap in its own comments with the count, rather than reporting a coverage it does not have: a check that silently omits a class is indistinguishable from one that found nothing in it.

Two reasons, both local. Five sit on `verdict` lines, which `docs/conventions/code.md` forbids tidying because the line states a prediction the harness scores. And `src/gl-fwd.c` emits a string whose spelling `docs/diagnostics.md` documents as the debug line a reader greps for, so emitter and matcher change together or not at all.

## Scope of the file list

Both checks take their inputs from version control rather than walking the filesystem. A file this repository does not track is one it does not author, so it is not scanned and does not need naming. A hardcoded list of directories to skip drifts from what is actually tracked, and each stale entry becomes a rule about a path that may not exist.

## Measured

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` and `sh scripts/check-charset.sh` both pass over 124 tracked files.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 12 gates, up from 8. Four are new: a dash refused, the wrapped form refused, a banned character refused, and the two code-span exemptions still applying.

`check-drift.sh` section 5 loses its dead ` -- ` delimiter handling. It split a TODO status from a trailing pointer clause on a punctuation dash, which the rule now refuses and which no entry writes any more. All 15 entries still reconcile against `TODO/INDEX.md`.

The diff touches no file under `src/`, `tests/` or `experiments/`.

title: Replace non-ASCII characters and dashes used as punctuation
body:
Mechanical text substitution across the tracked tree. No rule, no check and no judgement about what a comment should say lands here: those are the next change in the stack. This one exists so that the checks arriving next can be armed over the whole tree at once instead of over a list of paths that grows.

## What changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| characters outside ASCII that are not one of the five markers | 76, in 11 files | 0 |
| the five markers themselves | 697 | 697, untouched |
| dashes used as punctuation, Markdown prose | 216 | 0 |
| dashes used as punctuation, C comments | 133 | 0 |
| dashes used as punctuation, shell, YAML, Python and Makefile comments | 144 | 0 |

`docs/conventions/prose.md` already forbade both. The tree did not comply, including `prose.md` itself, which used the spelling it bans three times.

Replacements follow the four rewrites `prose.md` already names: a full stop, a colon, a pair of commas, or deletion. Characters were replaced by name: `.` for a middle dot used as a list separator, the word `section` for the section sign, `>=`, and `to` for a range.

## What deliberately did not change

- **The history record's wording.** `HISTORY/` records what was true when it was written, and the repository already excludes it from the one-fact-one-home gate for that reason. Its 98 dashes are untouched. Two characters were normalised, both `>=`, because substituting a character does not alter a sentence.
- **Prose inside strings a program prints**, 106 occurrences. Five sit on `verdict` lines, which `docs/conventions/code.md` forbids tidying. One is `src/gl-fwd.c`'s `"target %s -- %s\n"`, whose spelling `docs/diagnostics.md` documents as the debug line a reader greps for: emitter and matcher change together or not at all.
- **`src/runtime-select.c:36`**, which documents its own CLI as `runtime-select -- CMD [ARGS...]`. That dash is the end-of-options separator, not punctuation.
- **Section banner lines** such as `# ----- name --`, which are dividers rather than sentences.

## Two things found while doing it

**A dash that was load-bearing.** `scripts/check-drift.sh` section 5 splits a TODO status from a trailing pointer clause with `sub(/ -- .*/, "", s)`. Rewriting that clause as prose broke the INDEX reconciliation check. T-03's pointer is now its own bullet, so the status line carries the status and nothing else.

**A dash the ratchet could never see.** Section 4 matches ` -- ` with a trailing space, so a paragraph that wrapped straight after the dash was never counted. 17 such occurrences were in the tree. They are cleared here, and the next change teaches the check to catch them.

## Generated files

`src/forward-shim.c` was regenerated from `tools/gen_forward_shim.py` after the generator's own comments were fixed, and the regenerated output differs only in comments.

`src/gl-fwd-gl.h`, `src/gl-fwd-egl.h` and `src/gl-fwd-gles2.h` needed one header line each. Regenerating them requires an AppDir that this machine does not have, so the line was edited to exactly what the generator now emits. `make gl-syms-check` in the AppImage suite is what confirms that, and it is the reason the edit is safe to make by hand rather than an exception to the rule.

## Measured

`sh scripts/run-evidence.sh` reports 53 of 53 MATCH, identical case for case to the same suite on `main` at `df11f5fb`.

`sh scripts/check-drift.sh` passes. The dash pin fell from 216 to 0, lowered in this change as section 4 requires.

`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves all 8 plantable gates, including `the dash ratchet refuses a new dash` against the new pin.

`sh scripts/run-appimage.sh` did not run, here or on `main`. It refuses to start because the pinned upstream `demo.AppImage` no longer matches: expected `d77a01eb`, arrived `b4d5fdc4`. That is pre-existing, and re-pinning is a deliberate reviewed act rather than something to fold into this change.

title: Make aarch64 real, add the release, and rewrite the front-door documents
body:
Makes aarch64 real, adds the release, and rewrites the front-door documents.

## The baseline this started from

CI had run once. x86-64 was green end to end; **every aarch64 job failed**, and
`secret-sweep` was red on every run including every bot pull request.
`TODO/PROGRESS.md` said CI had never run, which was stale.

## 1. aarch64

**`-fcf-protection=full` is x86-only**, and on aarch64 gcc it is a hard error,
so both aarch64 builds died at the first shim. The flag is now selected from
`$(CC) -dumpmachine` rather than `uname -m`, because the aarch64 artefacts are
cross-compiled and only the compiler knows what it is targeting. Measured both
sides: x86-64 `gl-fwd.so` carries 3478 `endbr64`, aarch64 carries 0.

**Fifteen hardcoded x86-64 names across four scripts**, not the one path the
failure reported. `scripts/suite-lib.sh` claimed the loader name, the musl
soname and the two asset URLs "all four derive from `uname -m`". Two of the
four did. Each stage now derives the loader, the triplet, the `/lib64` versus
`/lib` fallback and the musl soname, and refuses an architecture it has no row
for. ⛔ E48's needle **was** the musl soname as a literal, so it moved in the
same edit.

**Three real aarch64 findings the ARM runner surfaced**, all measured:

- **E16** passed a literal `1` as `__xstat`'s version argument, which is
  x86-64's value. Under qemu-user on aarch64, `__xstat(0)` fills the struct and
  `__xstat(1)` returns `EINVAL`. glibc 2.31 exports no usable macro for it on
  either target, measured with `gcc -E -dM`.
- **E22** measures a version-binding trap that needs `pthread_cond_init` at two
  symbol versions. x86-64 has two, aarch64 has one. It now SKIPs, naming the
  count it found.
- ⭐ **E23 skips with it**, and that is the finding rather than the tidy-up.
  E22's own comment says E23 measures nothing once the trap is gone, and E23
  had been reporting MATCH on the ARM runner while asserting nothing.
- **E58** is hand-written x86-64 machine code. It SKIPs, and names E69-E73 and
  E76 as where the real aarch64 trampolines are measured.

**Result:** every aarch64 job green, and both totals re-measured on one commit
in run 32952579071: **53/53 on x86-64 and 50/50 on aarch64**. They differ by
exactly the three cases aarch64 skips, each naming the capability it lacks.
`docs/REPORT.md` section 8 is their one home.

## 2. T-17, corrected

T-17 recorded that no Debian gcc emits the IBT property note, tried three ways
including `-Wl,-z,ibt,-z,shstk`. Re-measured on bullseye 10.2, bookworm 12.2 and
trixie 14.2: **all three do emit it with that flag.**

The finding underneath is that the note would be **false**. `_init` and `_fini`
come from glibc's `crti.o`/`crtn.o`, `ld.so` reaches them through `DT_INIT` and
`DT_FINI`, and neither begins with `endbr64`. `crti.o` carries no property on
any of the three images, which is exactly why the linker's AND drops it. The
absence is the linker being right. `verify-artifacts.sh` now refuses an x86-64
build with no `endbr64`, which is the property the flag actually delivers.

## 3. The release (T-18)

`scripts/build.sh` already enforces the floor, so the workflow calls it rather
than carrying a second rule. `scripts/package-release.sh` **verifies rather
than recomputes**: every checksum is already in `build-manifest.json` and the
file is checked against it. ⛔ Neither archive contains a directory, and that
is asserted, not assumed. `scripts/release-notes.sh` generates the body from
the manifests; nothing in it is typed at release time.

Only a tag publishes. The pull request rule is **checked**: a tag whose commit
is not an ancestor of the default branch never went through review, and
publishing refuses. A pull request touching the release path runs the whole
thing up to the publish, so it is proven before it is needed.

## 4. secret-sweep, and a real scanner

Two categories, both false positives, no credential. Narrowed at the call site
in `scripts/sweep-known-benign.sh`, **by name**, with every other category
still fatal. The email category is also re-checked by shape, so a genuine
address still turns it red. Three-sided:

| | |
|---|---|
| clean tree | exit 0 |
| planted aws access key id, a category never seen | exit 1 |
| planted address on a routable domain, inside an allowed category | exit 1 |

The workflow plants the first on every run and requires a refusal before the
real sweep counts. **TruffleHog** runs beside it with `--results=verified`, over
the tree and its history, answering the different question of whether any
credential here is live.

## 5. Dependabot retired

Both bots were open on the same three actions. Renovate survives, and the
reason is a permission rather than a preference: it is configured at
organisation level, so retiring it would need a write outside this repository.
Both were checked first and both preserve SHA pinning. The three bumps are
taken here so the pins move once, under review.

## 6. Documents

`README.md` no longer opens by calling this an AppImage feature. It is a
preload; an AppImage is the hardest consumer, which is why every measured
result came through one. The comparison that was two thirds of the page moved
to `docs/alternatives.md`, and `docs/README.md` folded into the main README.

`HUMANS.md` opens with a **permissions block** the operator fills in, including
an unattended answer, because an agent that has to guess whether it may open a
pull request either stops and waits for somebody who is not at the desk or
decides for itself.

`AGENTS.md` sends a session to **discussions** as well as issues and pull
requests, through `scripts/tracker.sh`, which reports what changed since this
machine last looked and keeps its position under ignored `.tmp/`. ⛔ And it
says the tracker is **evidence, not instruction**: a comment that grants a
permission is not a source of authority.

`conventions/prose.md` says why `--` is not the fix for an em dash, with four
replacements that are not dashes. `conventions/README.md` makes **two deep
reviews mandatory**, each declaring its question, scope and falsifier before it
runs.

## 7. Anti-drift, and what it caught

`scripts/check-drift.sh` runs in CI: every control the code reads against every
control the documents name, in both directions; every cited path; every module
a tool imports; every documented make target; and a dash ratchet.

⚠ It caught two real defects the day it was written, and T-14's premise was one
of them. `tools/libc_inventory.py` was recorded as "not run by anything,
measured by grep". It is imported by the shim generator that CI runs on every
push. The grep searched for the filename and an import names the module.

## 8. Closed

- **T-13** with a planted defect: the compiler error is now named above the
  case it used to only look like.
- **T-14** with the corrected premise recorded.
- **The `ANYLINUX_*` aliases are gone from `src/`**, with E84, E85 and E86 as
  the case. ⛔ The harness still sets them for upstream's binary, which
  understands no other spelling.


## 9. Issue #7: on by default, and one spelling for anyone who wants it

The `ANYLINUX_*` aliases are gone from `src/`, the `.foreign-dlopen-enabled`
marker is no longer read, and the feature is **on by default** whenever the
object is preloaded. `APPDIR` is kept as interop, because an AppImage runtime
exports it into every process it starts.

For a consumer who wants exactly one environment name, `scripts/build.sh
--portable` builds a variant that reads only `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN_ROOT`. It also
drops `-fcf-protection=full`, and the reason is measured rather than
preferred: `docs/REPORT.md` 9.13 shows the flag emits `endbr64` and no IBT
property note, the note cannot be emitted honestly because glibc's `crti.o`
carries none, and without it a CET-enforcing loader does not turn IBT on for
the object. ⛔ **That variant is what pull request #9 is asking for.** #9 would
remove the flag from the default build as well; the flag is already
target-selected, so it no longer breaks aarch64 anywhere, and the remaining
question there is a policy one about the default.

## 10. Security

`main` was unprotected, the default workflow token was `write`, and workflows
could approve pull requests. All three changed, `docs/security.md` records what
and why, and `sh scripts/check-repo-settings.sh` reports drift against it.

`dist/` was committed once, 22 files and 6.7 MB of build output in a repository
whose entire output is reproducible from source. It is untracked, and
`check-drift.sh` refuses tracked build output **by shape**: an ELF object, an
archive or an AppImage has no business being tracked here whatever it is
called. Planted both ways, both exit 1.

## 11. Three deep review passes

`docs/conventions/README.md` requires two, each declaring its question, scope
and falsifier before it runs, and two that ask the same question do not count.
Three were run.

**Pass 1, can every guard added here refuse?** ⛔ Two could not, and neither
was broken in the way it looked. The **dash ratchet** was recorded as failing
to fire on a planted dash. The counter was never wrong: the refusal condition
was `count > pin`, the pin was set once and nothing ever lowered it, and the
tree had drifted eight under, so the plant landed inside the slack. The pin is
exact now, a fall refuses too, and the counter stops counting the `--` that
the prose rule explicitly exempts inside a code block. The **cited-path check**
could not see a path cited in front of a command, which is this repository's
commonest citation shape, and so it never noticed that `conventions/prose.md`
named a ratchet script that has never existed. 80 paths checked before, 87
after. `docs/REPORT.md` 9.14.

**Pass 2, what did this branch stop measuring?** ⛔ The branch added a real ARM
runner saying in the matrix that `qemu` "emulates the instructions and not a
memory model", and section P went on running the aarch64 trampolines under
`qemu-aarch64-static` **on aarch64 silicon**. It picks its vehicle from the
host now and prints which it used. Also: the marker was removed and four
documents went on calling it load-bearing, one of them the comment explaining
why E40 passes. E40 passes for a stronger reason than the one written down,
which is why nobody noticed. 9.16.

**Pass 3, does every claim added here hold when the command is run?** ⛔ The
"print a MISMATCH in full" fix that T-13 closed was in one harness and not the
other, and it was found by the failure it describes: E49 went MISMATCH with one
truncated line of preamble. The corpus cases were the same shape a third time,
reporting `0 / 0 load` with the reason in a stderr sent to `/dev/null`. And
`TODO/INDEX.md` listed two entries as open and partially done that declare
themselves DONE; `check-drift.sh` now compares every entry's status against its
row. 9.17.

## 12. The AppImage suite, run for the first time

It had never completed on either architecture. It does now, and getting there
produced the findings this pull request is least able to resolve on its own.

**The pin did its job and the artefact moved.** Both AppImages are pinned by
sha256 against a **mutable** `demo` tag, and the assets were replaced twice in
two minutes. ⛔ There is no immutable release to pin to instead: both the
upstream and the fork publish exactly one release each and both are tagged
`demo`. Mirroring into this repository is refused by the tracked-build-output
rule above. So re-pinning is a maintained act, and the refusal now says which
of three things disagreed: the pin, the bytes that arrived, or the digest the
release publishes today. All five paths proven, four refusals exit 1.

**`gtk4-demo` now comes from `pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages`**, the upstream.
⚠ The demo AppImage cannot: `vkcube+glxgears-host-drivers-demo-*` is published
only by the fork, `host-drivers` appears 0 times in the upstream's code, and
the upstream's `vkcube+glxgears-demo-*` is the build that BUNDLES its drivers,
which is the opposite of what this suite measures.

**Upstream adopted this project, and the AppDir changed shape.**
`lib/foreign-dlopen.so` is gone; `lib/cross-libc-dlopen.so` is in its place,
and `lib/` also ships this project's `gl-fwd.so`, `egl-fwd.so` and
`gles-fwd.so`, all six named in `.preload`. The dispatcher slot is read out of
the AppDir now instead of being spelled by either side. ⛔ The quieter half: the
shipped `.preload` was the baseline every case restored from before appending
the shim under test, so every case whose point is a shim's **absence** would
have run with upstream's copy of it present and passed silently. There are two
files now, and what the baseline drops is printed on every extraction.

**`tests/bindprobe.c` builds on aarch64.** It refused at compile time because
`scan_relocs()` knew two relocation numbers and both were x86-64's.

## 13. aarch64 has a live ABI hazard x86-64 does not

⛔ **The finding this branch exists to have made possible, and it needed real
ARM silicon.** On aarch64 musl's `pthread_mutex_t` is 40 bytes and glibc's is
48. A musl object that allocates one with its own `sizeof` and calls
`pthread_mutex_init` gets **glibc's** init, because making every reference
resolve to one libc is the whole point, and glibc writes 48 bytes into 40. ⚠ No
crossing is involved: the overflow is inside the musl object, on its own
allocation, and it happens because the loader did exactly its job.

It surfaced as E49 aborting with SIGABRT on every aarch64 host stage, and three
chained reporting defects had to be fixed before it was even legible:

| where | what was hidden |
|---|---|
| `40-appimage.sh`'s `run()` | a MISMATCH printed a 96-column summary; `30-run-tests.sh` has printed the whole output since T-13 closed |
| the corpus cases | `0 / 0 load` with the cause in a `2>/dev/null` |
| `abi-host.c` T1.6 | the abort itself, which ended the run before the hazard scan |

⚠ **The first fix for it was in the wrong place and is recorded rather than
quietly corrected**, because the failure it produced looked like success: it
guarded the host's lock, printed the hazard in full, moved E50 from 0 hazards
to 1, and the process still died at the same `free()` with the same `exit 134`.
The guard belongs around the CALL.

Proven by reproducing the abort on x86-64 rather than by reasoning: against the
same planted guest, the guard around the lock gives exit 134 and the guard
around the call gives exit 0 and 26 checks passed. Against an honest same-libc
guest the crossing is still performed. ⚠ Whether the overflow is *noticed*
depends on allocator rounding; the write is real either way, and a silent one
is the worse outcome.

**Both hazard counts now measured**, run 32957101324: 2 on x86-64, 3 on
aarch64. E50 reads the condition out of `abi-host`'s own size table rather than
carrying a per-architecture number. Section 11 carries the limitation as known
and unfixed.

## 14. What the completed suite found that nothing else could

⭐ **`sh scripts/verify-gates.sh` proves 8 gates, `sh scripts/check-drift.sh`
has six sections, and every new check was planted and seen to refuse.** The
dash ratchet caught its own author within the hour of being armed: a doc
rewrite dropped one prose dash, the count fell, and the check refused the
commit until the pin came down with it.

`package-release.sh`'s two refusals were planted for the first time, against a
synthetic build directory: a manifest that disagrees with its files, and a
`tar` invocation changed to nest. Both exit 1, a clean one exits 0.

⛔ **And the corpus sweep dies partway on two hosts**, which had been invisible
behind `2>/dev/null`: a segmentation fault through 298 libraries on Alpine, and
a library that calls the process dead on load on Debian. Both truncate the
result to nothing, so E33 and E34 were being scored against a total of zero.
That is T-15's premise, which until now was inferred from reading another
project. ⚠ The Alpine fault is **not yet attributed to a library**.

## What is not done, and what needs a decision

- ⛔ **The A/B's control arm no longer contrasts.** E30 and E37a assert the
  as-shipped arm reports `NO-DEVICES` and `zero accessible devices`. It now
  finds a device, because the shipped dispatcher is this project. Flipping the
  predictions would turn two controls into two cases that pass whatever the
  shim does. The honest control for "the feature is absent" is an AppDir with
  no dispatcher in `.preload`, and choosing that changes what the suite claims
  about upstream. Left open deliberately. 9.17.
- ⛔ **The Alpine corpus segmentation fault is unattributed.** Nobody should
  assume it belongs to the corpus rather than to this project until it is.
- **No release has been cut**, and the publish path cannot be proven until
  `release.yml` is on the default branch. `release.yml`'s ancestor refusal is
  the one guard in the release family still unproven, because firing it needs a
  tag and pushing one publishes.
- **`docs/ground-truth.md`'s stub export counts and soname total** are labelled
  UNVERIFIED rather than corrected: four counting methods were tried against
  the new binary and none reproduces the recorded four, every one of the
  closest method's numbers is exactly one low, and the old binary is gone so
  method and artefact cannot be separated.
- **T-11 and T-16.** T-12 is answered for the cases that end on their own and
  unanswerable, as instrumented, for the two that are killed on purpose. T-10's
  entry now names which gates have been seen to refuse and which four still
  need a runner and a deliberate push.

title: Remove the .foreign-dlopen-enabled marker and enable the library by default
body:
## Summary

Drop the build-time opt-in marker mechanism (`CLD_MARKER_NAMES`, i.e. `.cross-libc-dlopen-enabled` and `.foreign-dlopen-enabled`), the deprecated `ANYLINUX_*` env aliases, and the `APPDIR` root handling. The library should be **enabled by default** when preloaded, with only an environment variable to **disable** it.

## Why

These markers and aliases are leftover from when this code was going to be deeply integrated into `Anylinux-AppImages` (as `foreign-dlopen.so`). It is now an independent, self-contained project, so that coupling no longer exists.

Preloading `cross-libc-dlopen.so` (and the `*-fwd.so` shims) is an explicit, deliberate act by the consumer. Requiring an opt-in marker or `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN=1` on top of that adds a silent-failure footgun: a consumer that preloads the object but forgets the marker/env gets a build that does nothing and gives no hint why. Defaulting to enabled removes that entire class of failure.

## Current behaviour

`cross_libc_dlopen_mode()` in `src/cross-libc-dlopen.c` only activates when either:

- `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN=1` (or the deprecated `ANYLINUX_LIB_FOREIGN_DLOPEN=1`) is set, or
- one of the markers in `CLD_MARKER_NAMES` (`src/cld-env.h`) exists at the bundle root.

On top of that, the deprecated `ANYLINUX_*` spellings and `APPDIR` root handling are still read throughout `src/cld-env.h` (`cld_getenv`, `cld_root`).

## Proposed behaviour

- The library activates by default whenever it is preloaded.
- A single env variable, e.g. `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN=0`, disables it (`=1` can remain a no-op / force, or be dropped).
- Remove `CLD_MARKER_NAMES` and the marker-scanning block in `cross_libc_dlopen_mode()`.
- Remove the deprecated `ANYLINUX_*` env aliases from `src/cld-env.h` (`cld_getenv` and the `CLD_ENV_ROOT_ALT` / `APPDIR` fallback). `CROSS_LIBC_DLOPEN_ROOT` is the one spelling that stays.

## Scope of "similar code"

- `src/cld-env.h`: the `CLD_MARKER_NAMES` define, the `ANYLINUX_*` deprecated aliases in `cld_getenv()`, and `CLD_ENV_ROOT_ALT` (`APPDIR`).
- `src/cross-libc-dlopen.c`: the marker loop inside `cross_libc_dlopen_mode()`.
- Any remaining `ANYLINUX_*` / `APPDIR` reads elsewhere in `src/` (`runtime-select.c`, `gl-fwd.c`, etc.).
